x: Commentary on Sūrat Nūḥ (Noah), peace be upon him. In the name of God, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h

Indeed, We sent Noah to his people: “Warn your people before a painful punishment comes upon them” (1). He said: “My people, I am a clear warner to you (2): worship God, be mindful of Him, and obey me (3). He will forgive you some of your sins and grant you respite until an appointed term. When God’s appointed term comes, it cannot be delayed, if only you knew” (4).
God, exalted is His mention, says: “Indeed, We sent Noah”—Noah son of Lamech—“to his people, saying: Warn your people before a painful punishment comes upon them.”

He says: We sent him to them with the instruction: Warn your people. Some grammarians say that “that” is in the accusative, and others say it is in the genitive. I have already explained the reasons for each position and the correct view in what has preceded in this book, making repetition here unnecessary
n
. In the reported reading of ʿAbd Allāh, it is: “Indeed, We sent Noah to his people: ‘Warn your people’”—without “that”
n

. This is permissible because “sending” has the sense of “saying,” as if it said: We said to Noah, “Warn your people before a painful punishment comes upon them.” That painful punishment was the Flood with which God drowned them.

evidence.text: In the reported reading of ʿAbd Allāh, it is: “Indeed, We sent Noah to his people: ‘Warn your people’”—without “that” (2).

x: His saying, “He said: My people, I am a clear warner to you”: God, exalted is His mention, says: Noah said to his people, “My people, I am a clear warner to you.” I warn you of God’s punishment, so beware lest it descend upon you because of your disbelief in Him. “Clear” means: I have made my warning to you plain.

His saying, “Worship God, be mindful of Him, and obey me”: God, exalted is His mention, reports Noah’s words to his people: I am a clear warner to you, telling you to worship God. He says: I warn you and command you to worship God. “Be mindful of Him”: He says: Guard yourselves from His punishment by believing in Him and acting in obedience to Him. “And obey me”: He says: Follow what I command you and accept my counsel.

c: Bishr related to us: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah,
m: concerning His saying, “Worship God, be mindful of Him, and obey me.” He said: God sent the messengers to call people to worship God alone, avoid what He has forbidden, and obey His command
n

x: His saying, “He will forgive you some of your sins”: He says: He will forgive you your sins. If someone asks, “Doesn’t ‘some of’ indicate a part?” the answer is that the preposition min has two uses and two positions. In one position, nothing else can take its place. In that case it indicates a part, as when you say, “I bought one of your slaves”: min is necessary here and means “some”—that is, “I bought some of your slaves,” or “I bought a slave from among your slaves.” In the other position, ʿan can take its place. When ʿan can replace it, it indicates the whole. For example, “My stomach hurts from food I ate” means “Food I ate made my stomach hurt”; ʿan can be used in place of min, and the sentence remains sound. So His saying, “He will forgive you some of your sins” means that He will pardon you and forgive you for them. It may also mean
n

that He will forgive you those sins for which He promised you punishment; as for those for which He did not promise punishment, His pardon of them has already preceded. That pardon has already preceded for you.

His saying, “and grant you respite until an appointed term”: He says: He will extend your lifespans and not destroy you with punishment, whether by drowning or otherwise, “until an appointed term”—a time He recorded in the Mother of the Book until which He would keep you, if you obeyed and worshipped Him. The authorities on interpretation said much the same as we have said.

m: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us: ʿĪsā related to us.

c: Al-Ḥārith also told me: al-Ḥasan related to us: Warqāʾ related to us,
m: both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, concerning God’s saying, “until an appointed term.” He said: The term already written down; when God’s appointed term comes, it cannot be delayed
n

x: His saying, “When God’s appointed term comes, it cannot be delayed, if only you knew”: God, exalted is His mention, says: The term God has written for His creatures in the Mother of the Book, when it comes to Him, will not be delayed beyond its appointed time or granted further respite. “If only you knew”: He says: If you knew that this is so, you would turn back in repentance to obedience to your Lord.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h

He said: “My Lord, I have called my people night and day (5), but my calling only increased their flight (6). Whenever I called them so that You might forgive them, they put their fingers in their ears, wrapped themselves in their garments, persisted, and grew arrogantly proud (7).”

God, exalted is His mention, says: Noah said this after he had delivered his Lord’s message to his people and warned them of what He had commanded him to warn them about, but they disobeyed him and rejected what he brought them from God: “My Lord, I have called my people night and day” to affirm Your oneness and worship You; I warned them of Your might and force.

“But my calling only increased their flight”: He says: My calling them to the truth to which You sent me, and which I summoned them to, only increased “their flight”—their turning away from it, fleeing from it, and rejecting it.

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us: Muḥammad b. Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatādah,
m: concerning His saying, “But my calling only increased their flight.” He said: We were told that a man would take his son to Noah and say to him: Beware of this man, lest he lead you astray. I see that my father took me to him when I was like you, and warned me as I am warning you now
n

x: His saying, “Whenever I called them so that You might forgive them, they put their fingers in their ears”: He, mighty and exalted, says: Whenever I called them to acknowledge Your oneness, obey You, and disavow the worship of anything besides You, so that You might forgive them if they did so, they put their fingers in their ears so they would not hear my call to them. “And wrapped themselves in their garments”: He says: They covered themselves with their garments so they would not hear my call. The authorities on interpretation said much the same as we have said. We mention who said this.

c: Yūnus told me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Ibn Zayd said
m: concerning His saying, “they put their fingers in their ears”: So that they would not hear Noah’s words.

x: His saying, “and persisted”: He says: They remained in the disbelief they were practicing and continued in it. The authorities on interpretation said much the same as we have said. We mention who said this.

c: Yūnus told me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Ibn Zayd said
m: concerning His saying, “and persisted.” He said: Persistence means their continuing in associationism
n
and disbelief.

x: His saying, “and grew arrogantly proud”: He says: They were arrogant and considered themselves too great to submit to the truth and accept the counsel to which I called them.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h

Then I called them openly (8); then I addressed them publicly and privately (9), saying: “Ask your Lord for forgiveness; He is ever forgiving (10). He will send the sky upon you in abundant rain (11).”
He says: Then I called them to what You commanded me to call them to, “openly”—plainly, without concealment.

m: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us: ʿĪsā related to us.

c: Al-Ḥārith also told me: al-Ḥasan related to us: Warqāʾ related to us,
m: both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, concerning His saying, “Then I called them openly.” He said: Open speech is speech delivered publicly
n

x: His saying, “Then I addressed them publicly and privately”: He says: I spoke plainly
n
to them and proclaimed the warning You commanded me to give.

m: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us: ʿĪsā related to us.

c: Al-Ḥārith also told me: al-Ḥasan related to us: Warqāʾ related to us,
m: both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, concerning His saying, “I addressed them publicly.” He said: I shouted to them
n

c: Ibn Ḥumayd related to us: Mihrān related to us, from Sufyān, from Mujāhid,
m: concerning “I addressed them publicly.” He said: I called out to them.

x: His saying, “and privately”: He says: I spoke to them privately, between me and them, in secret. The authorities on interpretation said much the same as we have said. We mention who said this.

m: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us: ʿĪsā related to us.

c: Al-Ḥārith also told me: al-Ḥasan related to us: Warqāʾ related to us,
m: both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, concerning His saying, “and privately.” He said: Between me and them (1).

x: His saying, “saying: Ask your Lord for forgiveness; He is ever forgiving”: He says: I told them: Ask your Lord to forgive your sins; repent to Him for your disbelief and your worship of gods besides Him; affirm His oneness and devote worship sincerely to Him, and He will forgive you. He is ever forgiving toward those who turn back to Him and repent of their sins.

His saying, “He will send the sky upon you in abundant rain”: He says: If you repent, affirm God’s oneness, and devote worship sincerely to Him, your Lord will give you rain: He will send the sky upon you with abundant, continuous rain.

c: Yūnus b. ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told me: Sufyān informed us, from Muṭarrif, from al-Shaʿbī, who said:
m: ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb went out to pray for rain and did no more than ask forgiveness; then he returned. They said to him: Commander of the Faithful, we did not see you pray for rain! He said: I sought rain through the rain-bringing constellations of heaven
n

. Then he recited: “Ask your Lord for forgiveness; He is ever forgiving (10). He will send the sky upon you in abundant rain (11),” and recited the verse in Sūrat Hūd until he reached, “and increase you in strength upon your strength”
n

evidence.text: He will send the sky upon you in abundant rain (11),” and recited the verse in Sūrat Hūd until he reached, “and increase you in strength upon your strength” (2) [Q 11:52].

x: Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h
He will provide you with wealth and sons, make gardens for you, and make rivers for you (12). What is the matter with you that you do not hold God in due awe (13), when He created you in stages (14)?

His saying, “He will provide you with wealth and sons”: He says: Along with that, your Lord will give you wealth and sons, increase your numbers, and add to what you possess. “And make gardens for you”: He says: He will provide you with gardens. “And make rivers for you”: rivers from which you can water your gardens and fields. Noah said this to them because, according to what is reported, they loved wealth and children. We mention who said this.

c: Bishr related to us: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah,
m: concerning His saying, from “Then I called them openly” through “and make rivers for you.” He said: Noah saw a people whose necks were strained with eagerness for this world, and said: Come to obedience to God, for in it are the gains of this world and the Hereafter
n

x: His saying, “What is the matter with you that you do not hold God in due awe?” The authorities on interpretation differed about its meaning.
Some said: What is the matter with you that you do not recognize God’s greatness? We mention who said this.

c: ʿAlī told me: Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us: Muʿāwiyah related to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās,
m: concerning “What is the matter with you that you do not hold God in due awe?” He said: His greatness
n

c: Ibn Bashshār related to us: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to us: Sufyān related to us, from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid,
m: concerning the same verse. He said: You do not recognize God’s greatness.

c: Muḥammad b. Ḥumayd related to us: Mihrān related to us, from Sufyān,
m: with the same wording.

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us: ʿĪsā related to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ and Qays, from Mujāhid,
m: concerning “you do not hold God in due awe.” He said: You do not care about God’s greatness
n

c: Abū Kurayb related to us: ʿUmar b. ʿUbayd related to us, from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid,
m: concerning the same verse. He said: They did not care about God’s greatness.

c: I was told by al-Ḥusayn:
m: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd related to us: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say concerning “you do not hold God in due awe”: It means His greatness.

c: Ibn Ḥumayd related to us: Jarīr related to us, from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid,
m: concerning the same verse. He said: You do not care about the greatness of your Lord. “Hope” can mean expectation and fear
n

x: Others said that it means: You do not venerate God with the veneration due to Him. We mention who said this.

c: Salm b. Junādah told me: Abū Muʿāwiyah related to us, from Ismāʿīl b.
m: Sumayʿ, from Muslim al-Baṭīn, from Saʿīd b. Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning “What is the matter with you that you do not hold God in due awe?” He said: What is the matter with you that you do not venerate God as He deserves to be venerated?
n

x: Others said: What is the matter with you that you do not know God’s greatness? We mention who said this.

c: Muḥammad b. Saʿd told me: My father related to me; my uncle related to me; my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās,
m: concerning the verse. He said: What is the matter with you that you do not know God’s greatness?
n

x: Others said instead: What is the matter with you that you do not expect a consequence from God? We mention who said this.

c: Bishr related to us: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah,
m: concerning the verse. He said: That is, a consequence.

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatādah,
m: concerning the same verse. He said: You do not expect a consequence from God
n

x: Others said instead: What is the matter with you that you do not hope for obedience to God? We mention who said this.

c: Yūnus told me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Ibn Zayd said
m: concerning God’s saying, “What is the matter with you that you do not hold God in due awe?” He said: “Due awe” means obedience. In our view, the soundest interpretation is: What is the matter with you that you do not fear God’s greatness? The Arabs may use “hope” in the sense of “fear” when it is accompanied by a negation, as Abū Dhūʾayb said
n
: “When bees sting him, he does not fear their sting, and he turns aside from it among the nest of furious bees.” By “does not hope” he means “does not fear.”

x: His saying, “when He created you in stages”: He says: He created you in one state after another: first as a drop of fluid, then as a clinging clot, then as a morsel of flesh. The authorities on interpretation said much the same as we have said.

c: ʿAlī told me: Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us: Muʿāwiyah related to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās,
m: concerning His saying, “when He created you in stages.” He said: A drop, then a clot, then a morsel of flesh
n

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us: ʿĪsā related to us, and al-Ḥārith told me: al-Ḥasan related to us: Warqāʾ related to us,
m: both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, concerning “when He created you in stages.” He said: From dust, then from a drop, then from a clot, and then through the stages He mentioned, until creation is complete.

c: Bishr related to us: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah,
m: concerning it. He said: Stage by stage: a drop, then a clot
n
, then bones; then He clothed the bones with flesh and brought him forth as another creation, causing hair to grow. Blessed is God, the best of creators.

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatādah,
m: concerning “when He created you in stages.” He said: A drop, then a clot, [then a morsel of flesh]
n
, then one form of creation after another
n

c: I was told by al-Ḥusayn:
m: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd related to us: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say concerning “He created you in stages”: From a drop, then a clot, then a morsel of flesh.

c: Yūnus told me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Ibn Zayd said
m: concerning His saying, “when He created you in stages”: First the drop; then a mixed drop, when blood mixes with it; then the blood overcomes the drop and it becomes a clot; then it becomes a morsel of flesh, then bones, and then the bones are clothed with flesh
n

c: Ibn Ḥumayd related to us: Jarīr related to us, from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid,
m: concerning His saying, “when He created you in stages.” He said: A drop, then a clot, one thing after another (1).

x: Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h

Do you not see how God created seven heavens in layers (15), placed the moon in them as a light, and made the sun a lamp (16)? God made you grow from the earth as plants (17), then He will return you to it and bring you forth again (18).
God, exalted is His mention, reports Noah’s words to his people, who associated partners with their Lord.

He argued with them using God’s proofs of His oneness: Do you not see, O people, so that you may reflect, “how God created seven heavens in layers”—one above another? Ṭibāq is a verbal noun from the expression ṭābaqtu, “I placed one thing over another.” It means: How God created seven heavens, each heaven placed above another.

His saying, “and placed the moon in them as a light”: He says: He placed the moon as a light in the seven heavens, “and made the sun” in them “a lamp.” The authorities on interpretation said much the same as we have said. We mention who said this.

c: Muḥammad b. Bashshār related to us: Muʿādh b. Hishām related to us: My father related to me, from Qatādah,
m: concerning “Do you not see how God created seven heavens in layers, placed the moon in them as a light, and made the sun a lamp.” He said: We were told that ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAmr b. al-ʿĀṣ used to say: The light of the sun and the moon is in the sky. If you wish, recite: “Do you not see how God created seven heavens in layers” through the end of the verse (2).

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatādah, from ʿAbd Allāh b.
m: ʿAmr, who said: The faces of the sun and moon are turned toward the heavens, and their backs toward the earth. I cite a verse from God’s Book as evidence: “He placed the moon in them as a light and made the sun a lamp” (1).

c: I was told by al-Ḥusayn:
m: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd related to us: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say concerning His saying, “He placed the moon in them as a light”: He created the moon on the day He created the seven heavens. Some grammarians of Baṣrah said that “He placed the moon in them as a light” is figurative, like saying, “I visited Banū Tamīm,” when one has visited only some of them. “God made you grow from the earth as plants”: He says: God brought you forth from the earth’s soil, creating you from it. “Then He will return you to it”: He says: He will return you to the earth as dust, making you as you were before He created you. “And bring you forth again”: He says: When He wills, He will bring you out of it alive—as you were human beings before He returned you to it and made you dust—bringing you forth again.

x: Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h

God made the earth for you as a spread (19), so that you may travel along its wide paths (20). Noah said: “My Lord, they disobeyed me and followed someone whose wealth and children only increased his loss (21). They devised a tremendous plot (22).”
God, exalted is His mention, reports Noah’s words to his people as he reminds them of his Lord’s blessings: God made the earth for you as a spread,
a place where you may settle and make your home. He made the earth for you as a spread on which you may settle and make your home.
His saying, “so that you may travel along its wide paths”: He says: So that you may travel along its branching, varied roads
n
. Fijāj is the plural of faj, meaning a road. The authorities on interpretation said much the same as we have said. We mention who said this.

c: Bishr related to us: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah,
m: concerning His saying, “so that you may travel along its wide paths.” He said: Roads and landmarks.

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatādah,
m: concerning it. He said: Roads
n

c: ʿAlī told me: Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us: Muʿāwiyah related to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās,
m: concerning His saying, “so that you may travel along its wide paths.” He said: Different roads
n

x: His saying, “Noah said: My Lord, they disobeyed me”: God, exalted is His mention, says: Noah said, “My Lord, my people disobeyed me”
n

. They opposed my command and rejected the guidance and right direction to which I called them. “And followed someone whose wealth and children only increased his loss”: He says: In their disobedience to me, they followed someone whose abundant wealth and children increased nothing but loss and distance from God, and departure from the straight path. The readers differed in how they read “his children.” Most of the readers of Madīnah read it with a fatḥah on both wāw and lām, and they read it that way throughout the Qurʾān. Most of the readers of Kūfah read it with a ḍammah on the wāw and a sukūn on the lām, and they read every occurrence of “children” from Sūrat Maryam to the end of the Qurʾān that way. Abū ʿAmr read it with a fatḥah on the wāw and lām everywhere in the Qurʾān
n
, except for this single occurrence in Sūrat Nūḥ, where he read it with a ḍammah on the wāw
n
. In our view, all of these are recognized readings, close in meaning, and whichever one a reader uses is correct.

evidence.text: The readers differed in how they read “his children.”
Most of the readers of Madīnah read it with a fatḥah on both wāw and lām, and they read it that way throughout the Qurʾān.
Most of the readers of Kūfah read it with a ḍammah on the wāw and a sukūn on the lām, and they read every occurrence of “children” from Sūrat Maryam to the end of the Qurʾān that way.
Abū ʿAmr read it with a fatḥah on the wāw and lām everywhere in the Qurʾān (1), except for this single occurrence in Sūrat Nūḥ, where he read it with a ḍammah on the wāw (2).

x: His saying, “They devised a tremendous plot”: He says: They devised a great plot. The authorities on interpretation said much the same as we have said. We mention who said this.

m: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us: ʿĪsā related to us.

c: Al-Ḥārith also told me: al-Ḥasan related to us: Warqāʾ related to us,
m: both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, concerning “tremendous.” He said: Great
n

c: Yūnus told me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Ibn Zayd said
m: concerning His saying, “They devised a tremendous plot”: A great one
n
, like His saying, “They will hear no idle talk there, nor any falsehood” [Q 78:35]
n

. As Ibn Zayd said, kubbār means “great.” The Arabs say ʿajīb and ʿujāb (“wondrous”), with a light or doubled consonant; they also say ḥusān and ḥussān, jumāl and jummāl, with a light or doubled consonant. The same applies to kabīr and kubbār.

x: Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h
They said: “Do not abandon your gods; do not abandon Wadd, Suwāʿ, Yaghūth, Yaʿūq, or Nasr” (23). They have led many astray. Do not increase the wrongdoers in anything but error (24).
God, exalted is His mention, reports Noah’s account of what his people said: “Do not abandon your gods, and do not abandon Wadd, Suwāʿ, Yaghūth, Yaʿūq, or Nasr.”
As reported, these were men among the descendants of Adam who became gods worshipped by the people of Noah. We have received the following account of them.

c: Ibn Ḥumayd related to us: Mihrān related to us, from Sufyān, from Mūsā, from Muḥammad b.
m: Qays, concerning “Yaghūth and Yaʿūq.” He said: They were righteous men among the descendants of Adam, with followers who took them as examples. When they died, their followers said: If we make images of them, it will make us more eager to worship when we remember them. So they made images of them. When those followers also died and another generation came, Iblīs insinuated to them: They only worshipped them, and through them rain was sent down. So they worshipped them (4).

c: Ibn Ḥumayd related to us: Mihrān related to us, from Sufyān, from his father, from ʿIkrimah, who said:
m: There were ten generations between Adam and Noah (5), all following Islam (6).

x: Others said that these were the names of the idols of Noah’s people.
We mention who said this.

c: Bishr related to us: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah,
m: concerning His saying, “Do not abandon your gods, and do not abandon Wadd, Suwāʿ, Yaghūth, Yaʿūq, or Nasr.” He said: Wadd belonged to this clan of Kalb at Dūmat al-Jandal; Suwāʿ belonged to Hudhayl at Ruhāṭ
n
; Yaghūth belonged to Banū Ghuṭayf of Murād at al-Jawf
n

in Sabaʾ; Yaʿūq belonged to Hamdān at Balkhaʿ; and Nasr belonged to Dhū al-Kalāʿ of Ḥimyar. Noah’s people worshipped these gods, and the Arabs worshipped them afterward. By God, they were nothing more than pieces of wood, clay, or stone.

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatādah,
m: concerning the same verse. He said: They were gods worshipped by Noah’s people, then the Arabs worshipped them afterward. Wadd belonged to Kalb at Dūmat al-Jandal; Suwāʿ belonged to Hudhayl; Yaghūth belonged to Banū Ghuṭayf of Murād at al-Jawf (3); Yaʿūq belonged to Hamdān; and Nasr belonged to Dhū al-Kalāʿ of Ḥimyar
n

c: ʿAlī told me: Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us: Muʿāwiyah related to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās,
m: concerning His saying, “Do not abandon Wadd, Suwāʿ, Yaghūth, Yaʿūq, or Nasr.” He said: These were idols worshipped in the time of Noah
n

c: I was told by al-Ḥusayn:
m: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd related to us: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say concerning “Yaghūth, Yaʿūq, and Nasr”: These were idols worshipped in the time of Noah
n

c: I was told by al-Ḥusayn:
m: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd related to us: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say concerning the same verse: They were gods in Yemen.

c: Yūnus told me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Ibn Zayd said
m: concerning His saying, “Yaghūth, Yaʿūq, and Nasr”: These were their gods whom they worshipped (1). The readers differed in how they read “Wadd.” Most of the readers of Madīnah read it with a ḍammah on the wāw, while most of the readers of Kūfah and Baṣrah read it with a fatḥah on the wāw
n

. In our view, both are recognized readings used by the readers of the cities, and whichever one a reader uses is correct. His saying, “They have led many astray”: God, exalted is His mention, reports Noah as saying: Many people have gone astray by worshipping these idols made in the images of the men named here. He attributed the act of leading astray to the idols because their worshippers went astray through them.

evidence.text: The readers differed in how they read “Wadd.”
Most of the readers of Madīnah read it with a ḍammah on the wāw, while most of the readers of Kūfah and Baṣrah read it with a fatḥah on the wāw (2).
In our view, both are recognized readings used by the readers of the cities, and whichever one a reader uses is correct.

x: His saying, “Do not increase the wrongdoers in anything but error”: He says: Do not increase those who wronged themselves by disbelieving in Our signs in anything but error—sealing their hearts so they cannot find the truth.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h

Because of their sins, they were drowned and then made to enter a Fire, and they found no helpers for themselves besides God (25). Noah said: “My Lord, do not leave upon the earth any inhabitant from among the unbelievers” (26).
By His saying, “Because of their sins,” He means: Because of their sins they were drowned.

The Arabs use mā as an extra particle in constructions expressing a conditional sense, as when one says, “Wherever you are, I will be,” or “Wherever you sit, I will sit.” The meaning is: Because of their sins, they were drowned.
Ibn Zayd held the following view, as Yūnus told me:

c: Ibn Wahb informed us: Ibn Zayd said
m: concerning His saying, “Because of their sins”: That is, for their sins they were drowned and then made to enter a Fire. Here the Arabs use the preposition bi (“because of”) as an explanatory particle.

c: Ibn Ḥumayd related to us: Mihrān related to us, from Sufyān,
m: concerning “Because of their sins they were drowned.” He said: They were drowned because of their sins. The readers differed in how they read “their sins.” Most of the readers of the cities, except Abū ʿAmr, read it with a hamzah and tāʾ. Abū ʿAmr read it as “their errors,” without a hamzah
n
. In our view these are both recognized readings, and a reader is correct with either one.

evidence.text: The readers differed in how they read “their sins.”
Most of the readers of the cities, except Abū ʿAmr, read it with a hamzah and tāʾ.
Abū ʿAmr read it as “their errors,” without a hamzah (3).

x: His saying, “and then made to enter a Fire”: Hell. “And they found no helpers for themselves besides God” means:

to exact retribution for them from those who did this to them or to shield them from what was done to them. His saying, “Noah said: My Lord, do not leave upon the earth any inhabitant from among the unbelievers”: God, exalted is His mention, says: Noah said, “My Lord, do not leave upon the earth any inhabitant from among the unbelievers” (1). Dayyār means someone who moves about the earth, going here and there. It is the form fayʿāl from dawār (“circling”): originally daywār; when the yāʾ and wāw came together and the yāʾ preceded a quiescent wāw, the wāw was assimilated into it, producing a doubled yāʾ, as in ḥayy al-qayyām, from qumtu, which is originally qaywām. The Arabs say: “There is no dayyār, no ʿarīb, no dawiyy (2), no whistling, and no one blowing on a firebrand (3),” by all of which they mean: There is no one there.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h

If You leave them, they will lead Your servants astray and beget none but a wicked ingrate (27). My Lord, forgive me, my parents, whoever enters my house as a believer, and the believing men and women. Do not increase the wrongdoers in anything but ruin (28).

God, exalted is His mention, reports Noah’s words in his prayer against his people: My Lord, if You leave the unbelievers alive on earth and do not destroy them with a punishment from You, they will lead Your servants who have believed in You astray and turn them away from Your path.

They will beget none but someone wicked in religion and ungrateful for Your blessings. Noah is reported to have said these words and made this supplication after his Lord revealed to him: “None of your people will believe except those who have already believed” [Q 11:36].
We mention who said this.

c: Bishr related to us: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah,
m: concerning His saying, “My Lord, do not leave upon the earth any inhabitant from among the unbelievers.” He said: By God, Noah did not pray against them until revelation came to him from heaven: “None of your people will believe except those who have already believed.” Then God’s Prophet Noah prayed against them, saying: “Noah said: My Lord, do not leave upon the earth any inhabitant from among the unbelievers (26). If You leave them, they will lead Your servants astray and beget none but a wicked ingrate.” Then he offered a general supplication, saying: “My Lord, forgive me, my parents, whoever enters my house as a believer, and the believing men and women,” through “ruin.”

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, who said:
m: Qatādah recited “Do not leave upon the earth any inhabitant from among the unbelievers,” then mentioned something similar (1). His saying, “My Lord, forgive me and my parents”: He says: My Lord, pardon me and cover my sins, and those of my parents. “And whoever enters my house as a believer”: He says: Whoever enters my mosque and place of prayer to pray, “as a believer”—that is, affirming the obligation You have imposed upon him. The authorities on interpretation said much the same as we have said concerning “whoever enters my house as a believer.” We mention who said this.

c: Bishr b. Ādam related to us: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Mahdī related to us: Sufyān related to us, from Abū Sinān,
m: [from Thābit] (2), from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, concerning “whoever enters my house as a believer.” He said: My mosque (3).

c: Ibn Ḥumayd related to us: Mihrān related to us: Sufyān related to us
m: (4), from Abū Sinān Saʿīd, from

x: al-Ḍaḥḥāk, with the same wording. His saying, “and the believing men and women”: He says: And those men and women who affirm Your oneness.

His saying, “Do not increase the wrongdoers in anything but ruin”: He says: Do not increase those who wronged themselves through disbelief in anything but loss. The authorities on interpretation said much the same as we have said. We mention who said this.

m: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us: ʿĪsā related to us.

c: Al-Ḥārith also told me: al-Ḥasan related to us: Warqāʾ related to us,
m: both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, concerning “in anything but ruin.” He said: Loss (1). I have already explained the meaning of “I was ruined” with supporting evidence and the statements of the authorities on interpretation, making repetition here unnecessary (2).

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us: Ibn Thawr related to us: Maʿmar said: al-Aʿmash related to us, from Mujāhid, who said:
m: They used to beat Noah until he fainted; when he came to, he would say: My Lord, forgive my people, for they do not know (3). This concludes the interpretation of Sūrat Nūḥ, peace be upon him.

x: His saying, “Do not increase the wrongdoers in anything but ruin”: He says: Do not increase those who wronged themselves through disbelief in anything but loss. The authorities on interpretation said much the same as we have said. We mention who said this.

m: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us: ʿĪsā related to us.

c: Al-Ḥārith also told me: al-Ḥasan related to us: Warqāʾ related to us,
m: both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, concerning “in anything but ruin.” He said: Loss
n
. I have already explained the meaning of “I was ruined” with supporting evidence and the statements of the authorities on interpretation, making repetition here unnecessary
n

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us: Ibn Thawr related to us: Maʿmar said: al-Aʿmash related to us, from Mujāhid, who said:
m: They used to beat Noah until he fainted; when he came to, he would say: My Lord, forgive my people, for they do not know
n
. This concludes the interpretation of Sūrat Nūḥ, peace be upon him.

notes.en: Majādiḥ is the plural of majdah, a stick with a forked head used to stir drinks, sometimes with three prongs. Al-majdah is also the name of a star, one of the lunar mansions that the Arabs took as indicating rain. Thus asking forgiveness was likened to those stars, addressing them in terms familiar to them, not affirming the influence of stars. See al-Nihāyah, 1:243.

notes.en: Manuscripts Ṣ, T1, T2, and T3 read “dabī.” Al-dawiyy is an attribution to al-daww, the wide open desert, a region of Arabia between Baṣrah and al-Yamāmah. Their expression “There is no dawiyy there” means there is no one who inhabits the desert. See Lisān al-ʿArab (root d-w-w).
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ت 2، ت 3: "دبي". والدَّوِّىُّ منسوب إلى الدَّوِّ، وهى الفلاة الواسعة، وهى أرض من أرض العرب بين البصرة واليمامة. وقولهم: ما بها دَوِّى. أى ما بها أحد ممن يسكن الدو. ينظر اللسان (د و و).

notes.en: Al-ḍaramah means “fire.” Al-Wasīṭ (root ḍ-r-m).
notes.ar: الضَّرَمة: النار. الوسيط (ض ر م).

notes.en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq included it in his Tafsīr, 2:320, from Maʿmar, with this chain. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthūr, 6:270, to ʿAbd b. Ḥumayd and Ibn al-Mundhir.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق فى تفسيره 2/ 320 عن معمر به. وعزاه السيوطى فى الدر المنثور 6/ 270 إلى عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر.

notes.en: Omitted in manuscript M. Thābit is Ibn Jābān. See his biographical entry in al-Jarḥ wa-l-Taʿdīl, 2:450.
notes.ar: سقط من: م. وثابت هو ابن جابان. تنظر ترجمته في الجرح والتعديل 2/ 450.

notes.en: Ibn Kathīr mentioned it in his Tafsīr, 8:264. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthūr, 6:270, to Ibn al-Mundhir.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 8/ 264. وعزاه السيوطى فى الدر المنثور 6/ 270 إلى ابن المنذر.

notes.en: The manuscripts add “from Abū Salamah” after it. See the earlier discussion, 13:212, 216–217, and 19:590.
notes.ar: بعده في النسخ: "عن أبي سلمة". وينظر ما تقدم في 13/ 212، 216، 217، 19/ 590.

notes.en: Ibn Kathīr mentioned it in his Tafsīr, 8:264. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthūr, 6:270, to ʿAbd b. Ḥumayd and Ibn al-Mundhir.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 8/ 264. وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 270 إلى عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر.

notes.en: See the earlier discussion, 10:411–412 and 14:504–505.
